Prohibitionism Hit On Three Fronts: The New York Times Flirts With Heresy on Prohibition,
The States Support Medical Marijuana and Hemp. -- Analysis

Once again the Internet makes it possible to bring together four articles from different sources. Combining them shows the mounting opposition to the prohibitionist party line, which is duly noted in each.

Although most newspapers will not print these articles on medical marijuana and hemp, the fact that the AP and UPI moved them on their wires, and the AP hemp article was on the Yahoo News Index, means they will be widely read by opinion leaders.

The US News article on which it may have been based, is popular in the business community. It is generally prohibitionist in both its reporting and editorials.

While the New York Times editorial may not be seen outside of that one very important paper, it hits many opinion leaders – even in Washington, where there are mostly "opinion followers."

There is a journalistic term – "to spike a story" – which means to kill a completed story for non-journalistic "policy" reasons, usually meaning that the publisher doesn’t like it.

All of the major media now have many spikes full of stories reflecting badly on the past, present, and future of marijuana prohibition. The American people have not seen most of them, but the editors have.

Of course, the people show every sign of being ahead of the media and the politicians on the cannabis issues.

The question is simply how long it will take for the "leaders" to catch up with their "followers." It had better be soon, or they will have absolutely no credibility left. America’s elites are running on empty.

As the Times editorial reflects, people -- even including the Drug Czar -- are beginning to question the very high costs and meager results of the "drug war." The Times pulls back from the obvious conclusions, but it has laid out the case that something is seriously wrong, and it is okay to ask questions.

As the AP and UPI stories make clear, the demands for hemp and medical marijuana are coming from many different sources around the country.

I concluded long ago that the marijuana reform movement will not be able to end marijuana prohibition by itself, but it will not have to. Our job is to awaken the civil institutions to the danger at hand.

The New York Times just made a loud, rude noise in the corridors of power.
